units.translation: The Pythian god told Croesus, king of the Lydians, to beware (96 Hendess Orac. gr. 1877, 61): 'Croesus, by crossing the Halys, will destroy a great empire.' It is between the Syrians in Pontus and the Paphlagonians, discharging into the Pontus.
b. Halys: a river of Paphlagonia, flowing out near Sinope. Lg (P)
367-68a. They roar: they resound, they flow with a sound. Lg (P)
b. And after it the swift-flowing Iris: after the Halys the Iris flows nearby, being smaller than the Halys in size. 'With white' instead of 'with pure'.
c. Iris: a river of Paphlagonia. Lg

369-72a. And from there forward: from there, he says, as they proceed, there is a certain headland jutting out into the sea; and after rounding it, there is a gulf, into which he says the Thermodon flows down under the Themiscyrean headland, where the Amazons lived.
c. Thermodon: a river of the Paphlagonians. Lg

d. It flows: instead of 'it streams out'. It should be construed thus: the mouth of the Thermodon flows into a gulf. 'Divided' by antistrophe means 'scattered', 'flowing with force', as if: the river Thermodon, flowing through much land, streams out into a deep-eddying gulf at the Themiscyrean headland.
373-76a. And there the plain of Doeas: Doeas and Acmon were brothers; but of what father, it is not recorded, as Pherecydes says (3 fg 15 b J.).

Near the plain of Doeas, he says, there are three cities where the Amazons dwelt: Lycastia, Themiscyra, and Chadesia. The Chalybes are a Scythian people beyond the Thermodon, who discovered iron mines and toil at the working of them. They were called Chalybes from Chalybs, son of Ares. Callimachus also mentions them (fg 35c Schn. = Pap. Soc. Ital. 1092, 48 sq.): 'May the race of the Chalybes perish, who revealed the evil plant springing from the earth.'
b. Most wretched: most toilsome. Lg P

377-80. Beyond the Genetaean headland: the Genetaean headland, properly so called from the river Genetos, where there is a sanctuary of Zeus Xenios. And the Tibareni are a Scythian people neighboring the Chalybes. The Mossynoeci are also a Scythian people, having acquired their name from their way of life. For 'mossyni' are called wooden houses, which they used; and he himself, hinting at this, said that they inhabit a wooded land. At any rate, from 'mossyn', which means a wooden house, they were called Mossynoeci.

382-85a. You will land on a smooth island: on the rugged and lofty one. The island is called Aretias. On this island were the Stymphalian birds, driven from Stymphalus, a city of Arcadia, by Heracles. On this island, then, he says, land with all haste; for there some benefit will appear to you.
